Covariance matrix of the estimates

Source: R/vcov_cluster.R
vcov.flexCountReg.Rd

vcov() returns the covariance matrix chosen at fit time, or recomputes a Hessian-based, robust or cluster-robust one from the stored scores, without refitting.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
vcov(object, type = NULL, cluster = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

a fitted flexCountReg model.

type

NULL or "fit" (default): the covariance chosen at fit time (stderr). "hessian": the inverse of the negative Hessian. "robust": the sandwich with one independent unit per row, or per panel for panel models. "cluster": cluster-robust with the clusters in cluster.

cluster

for type = "cluster": a one-sided formula of the clustering variable(s) in the model's data (~ corridor; two or more variables, ~ corridor + year, give multiway clustering), their names, or a vector with one cluster id per row used in estimation.

...

not used.

Value

A square matrix with the parameter names as dimnames.

Details

Cluster-robust covariances use the scores of the model's independent units (rows, or panels for countreg_rp() with group_var, renb(), repois(), poislind_re()), summed within each cluster, with the small-sample factor \(G/(G-1)\) for \(G\) clusters. Clusters may be coarser than the panels (for example sites within corridors) but may not split a panel. Multiway clustering follows Cameron, Gelbach and Miller (2011). With frequency weights, a row with weight \(w\) stands for \(w\) observations in the same cluster.

The number of clusters is attached as the attribute "n_clusters". The scores and the bread are also available to the sandwich package through estfun.flexCountReg.

References

Cameron, A.C., Gelbach, J.B. and Miller, D.L. (2011). Robust inference with multiway clustering. Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, 29(2), 238-249.

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
m <- countreg(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength, data = washington_roads,
              family = "NB2", method = "BFGS")
sqrt(diag(vcov(m)))
#> (Intercept)      lnaadt    lnlength   ln(alpha) 
#>  0.44451075  0.05291691  0.06960363  0.23366292 
sqrt(diag(vcov(m, type = "cluster", cluster = ~ ID)))
#> (Intercept)      lnaadt    lnlength   ln(alpha) 
#>  0.58639184  0.06790319  0.08712895  0.24190144 
# }
